examples.solution_text:
(a) Join $A$ and $B$ to the centre $O$. The vertex is the middle letter, so the angle is **$\angle AOB$**.
(b) Join $A$ and $B$ to each circumference point. The angles are **$\angle ACB$** and **$\angle ADB$**.
(c) The arm endpoints are $A$ and $B$, so the chord is **$AB$**.
(d) $\angle CAB$ has vertex $A$, not $C$. To name the angle at $C$, put $C$ in the middle: $\angle ACB$.
(e) Chord $AB$ **subtends**, or forms, an angle when its endpoints are joined to the vertex.

(a) $R$ is on the short, minor arc $PQ$. The angle stands on the arc not containing $R$, so **$\angle PRQ$ stands on the major arc $PQ$**.
(b) $S$ is on the long, major arc $PQ$. The arc not containing $S$ is the short arc, so **$\angle PSQ$ stands on the minor arc $PQ$**.
(c) **No.** Both angles are subtended by chord $PQ$, but their vertices are on opposite arcs. Each angle stands on the arc opposite its own vertex.

(a) $M$ lies on the boundary of the major segment. Put the vertex $M$ between the endpoints: **$\angle KML$**.
(b) $N$ lies on the boundary of the minor segment. Put the vertex $N$ between the endpoints: **$\angle KNL$**.
(c) The arms join $K$ and $L$ to the centre $O$, so the angle is **$\angle KOL$**.
(d) The arm endpoints are $K$ and $L$, so the chord is **$KL$**.

examples.derivation: Chord KL lies at y=0.8, since K and L have polar angles 150° and 30° with radius 1.6. N at 85° lies on the minor arc above the chord; M at 260° lies on the major arc below it. The circumference angles in the major and minor segments are therefore ∠KML and ∠KNL. Joining K and L to centre O forms ∠KOL, whose arm endpoints identify chord KL. All required arms are drawn.
